Researchers map deep-sea vents

A team of oceanographers has completed the most detailed map yet of hydrothermal vents along a remote stretch of the mid-ocean ridge, using autonomous submarines that spent three weeks surveying the seafloor.

The vents, which release mineral-rich water heated by magma below the crust, host communities of organisms that live without sunlight. The new map identifies more than forty previously unknown vent fields.

Scientists say the data will help them understand how such ecosystems are distributed and how they might be affected by proposed deep-sea mining, which has drawn concern from conservation groups around the world.
